waves.notes: Parallel workers handled the high-risk hook fail-closed change and frontend markdown/CSP proof. Targeted hook and frontend checks passed before integration.

Web endpoint bundle landed with CORS allowlist, config validation/atomic write/audit, and device revoke re-proof/rate-limit/404 semantics. One repair pass added config audit logging and tightened the body cap.

what_slowed: The Rust dependency audit is already red on unmaintained transitive crates outside the edited endpoint, hook, and frontend files.
Device revoke hardening overlapped three backlog items, so the web endpoint bundle needed one integrated pass instead of independent workers.
process_fixes: Keep dependency-audit remediation as a dedicated next campaign; it needs dependency and policy decisions, not endpoint-local patches.
When a security ticket mentions audit logging in fix text but not acceptance, include it in the first pass.

how_to_run: cd crates/wisphive_web/frontend && npm test && npm run lint && npm run build
cargo deny check advisories bans sources

items.label: From a logged-in web session, save the config panel and confirm the config persists; try a non-Vite Origin preflight and confirm no wildcard CORS.
Use a bearer token to revoke a peer device: wrong password should 401, first valid revoke should 200, immediate second active revoke should 429.
Render hostile markdown-like agent output and confirm script/img/javascript payloads appear inert while normal https links still work.

rows.notes: Seven endpoint/hook/frontend security backlog items are agent-verified by tests, lint, frontend audit, and workspace gates. Keep the row yellow because cargo-deny advisories remain and mobile/LAN exposure has additional out-of-scope blockers.
